plate_findings.evidence: The caption states that follow-up CT revealed newly developed pneumatosis intestinalis in the ascending colon, and the circled intraluminal gas is visible.
The caption identifies the circled CT abnormality as transmural infarction, a listed synonym for the loss-of-wall-enhancement finding.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Initial non-contrast abdominal CT from a patient with acute ischemic colitis demonstrates diffuse colonic dilatation, circled in red. Colonic dilatation is not represented in the supplied finding vocabulary but is explicitly stated in the caption. [raw subtype: acute ischemic colitis] B: Follow-up CT in the same patient with acute ischemic colitis shows circled ascending-colon pneumatosis, explicitly interpreted as consistent with transmural infarction. This is a severe, fulminant manifestation of the target disease. [raw subtype: fulminant ischemic colitis with transmural infarction]

panels.figure_caption: Radiological progression of acute ischemic colitis during a hyperglycemic crisis. (A) Initial abdominal computed tomography (CT) obtained at emergency department presentation demonstrated diffuse colonic dilatation. (B) Follow-up CT performed 48 hours after admission revealing newly developed pneumatosis intestinalis in the ascending colon, consistent with transmural infarction (red dotted circle).
in_text_mentions: catastrophe, a non-contrast abdominal computed tomography (CT) was performed due to renal impairment. Imaging revealed ischemic change with pneumatosis intestinalis involving the ascending to proximal transverse colon, with associated findings suggestive of peritonitis (Figure 2). Urgent surgical consultation was obtained, and in the setting of clinical deterioration and evolving peritoneal signs, emergency operative intervention was undertaken. Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) was initiated preoperatively in view of progressive acute kidney injury and refractory metabolic acidosis.
